__comment: How to connect an AI assistant, linked from the home dashboard's third card. Markdown rather than HTML so the code blocks are selectable to copy. @@MCP_URL@@ is the one value that cannot be baked in -- it carries SERVER_NAME and DEBUG, both runtime settings -- so grafana/entrypoint.sh substitutes it into a writable copy of this file at container start, deriving it from the same GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL Grafana itself uses. MCP_PATH and GRAFANA_PATH are substituted at build time by grafana/render.sh.

# Add the MCP server to your AI

Your assistant can then search dashboards, run a panel's query, explain what a metric means
and build new dashboards — doing exactly what you are allowed to do, and nothing more.

### 1. Make yourself a token

Go to **Administration → Users and access → Service accounts**, click
**Add service account**, give it your own role (`Viewer`, `Editor` or `Admin`), then
**Add service account token** and copy the token.

The token carries your access, so treat it like a password. A `Viewer` token cannot change
anything, whoever uses it.

### 2. Point your assistant at this server

This is the address of this system, so the commands below are ready to copy as they stand.

**Claude Code** — one command:

```
claude mcp add --transport http ${APP_NAME} @@MCP_URL@@ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"
```

**Claude Desktop, Copilot, Cursor and others** — the same two values in the
configuration file:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "${APP_NAME}": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "@@MCP_URL@@",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }
    }
  }
}
```

### 3. Try it

Ask your assistant *"which dashboards exist here?"* or *"what is the server monitoring
dashboard showing?"*. If it answers, you are set up.

If it cannot connect, check that you copied the whole token, and that the address above is
the one you reach this page under — behind a different name or port, use that instead.

title: Add the MCP server to your AI
